title: Randy Moss returning to ESPN's 'NFL Countdown' 2 months after stepping away for cancer battle
text:
ESPN is recovering Randy Moss. (Photo by Simon Bruty/Sports Illustrated through Getty Images)
Randy Moss will return with ESPN on Sunday, just in time for the Super Bowl Lix.
The six times PRO Bowler returns to the study for “NFL countdown” before the clash between the chiefs of Kansas City and Philadelphia Eagles, Adam Schefter from ESPN announced Saturday .
Moss moved away from the program indefinitely in December, due to what was described as a “personal health challenge.” He had caught attention the previous week for wearing sunglasses in the study for an unrelated reason.
Later, Moss confirmed that his problem was cancer. He announced that he had successfully submitted complex surgery called whipple procedure to eliminate cancer cells, but said that chemotherapy and radiation treatment still required:
“I am a cancer survivor. Some difficult moments, of course, but, you know, we succeed. And that’s why I thank everyone,” Moss said.
Moss previously made a remote appearance during the Honors of the NFL on Thursday, announcing to the Campinnati Bengals field, Joe Burrow as the return player of the year.
There were a series of tributes towards Moss during their battle, even of their companions legends of Minnesota Vikings. He has talked about Touched, he feels all the support of family, friends and fans, and has also started selling hoodie and hoodies “ Team Moss: We go to moss cancer “To benefit cancer investigation.
